subject.title: update.run: pnpm prunes running dist before launchd plist rewrite → silent 51-day crash-loop

question: Should OpenClaw support gateway-initiated upgrades from pre-`v2026.5.18` managed installations with a retrofit-safe bootstrap, or declare that legacy versions must update from an outside shell?
rationale: The current handoff is correct for gateways that already contain it, but old shipped binaries cannot consume that logic before their first package mutation; choosing a retrofit mechanism versus a documented support boundary requires maintainer upgrade-policy judgment.

options.title: Add legacy upgrade bootstrap
options.body: Implement a narrowly guarded host-side or target-installer path that safely rewrites and verifies the managed service when a vulnerable old gateway initiates its first upgrade.

options.title: Require outside-shell upgrade
options.body: Declare pre-`v2026.5.18` gateway self-update unsupported, add prominent detection and recovery guidance where current surfaces can expose it, and direct users to update from a host shell.

recommendation.title: Add legacy upgrade bootstrap
recommendation.body: Implement a narrowly guarded host-side or target-installer path that safely rewrites and verifies the managed service when a vulnerable old gateway initiates its first upgrade.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad ownership across updater recovery, handoff verification, and merge decisions for this lifecycle surface.
